history.period: c. 400 years old, Mughal period (traditional account; UNVERIFIED)
history.summary: The Kamakhya Sthan of Purnia district at Krityanand Nagar, on the border of Rahua, Majra and Bhabanipur villages (CSV town 'Purnia' is approximate — the site is in Purnia district, several km from Purnia city). Local accounts call it 400 years old, built in the Mughal period, and claim it is older than Guwahati's Kamrup Kamakhya; the goddess is seated here in the form 'Kshem-karni'. Legends include healing of leprosy patients by the goddess's grace and the story of two girls, Sundari and Shyama, protected from the Mughals. Coordinates are from a place listing for 'Maa Kamakhya Sthan Bhawanipur Majra' and are approximate (verify). Media image is from the angdesh.com article on Kamakhya Mandir, Purnea.

name: Kamakshi Sthan Temple
town_description: Krityanand Nagar is a village in Purnia district, northeastern Bihar, known locally as Kamakhya Sthan; the temple stands near the meeting point of Rahua, Majra and Bhabanipur villages, in the fertile Kosi-Seemanchal belt.
